text:
Priya: Need a refreshed competitive card + 45min prep for the webinar workshop. Focus: two headline experiments, three benchmark callouts, and a 1-pager rebut sheet for SDRs.
Carlos: OK. Headline experiments: A) "Inference that fits your SLA and budget" B) "Stop picking between latency and cost". Which tests better for signup CTAs?
Nina: A is more enterprise-friendly; B has punch for dev communities. Let's A/B by audience segment.
Jared: Benchmarks: propose these three callouts: median latency under 512 tokens, p95 cost per token vs public LLM API, and failover time when a model variant is down. Keep claim language conservative.
Priya: Good. Draft soundbites: cloud AI platforms: "Broad managed services, variable inference economics" + support: "customers report variable p95 costs depending on mix". LLM APIs: "Fast to start, limited rollout controls" + support: "few provide canary/pinning features out of the box". Infra vendors: "You own infra, you still need a serving runtime" + support: "operators reimplement batching, cache, and quant selection."
Carlos: SDR ask: one-liner rebut for "We already spend on cloud infra": "Optimize spend with a serving layer that routes to cheapest compatible path; keep existing infra investments."
Nina: Add an objection path for "We need compliance": "Private deployment options with customer-managed VPC and KMS integrations."
Jared: For the webinar slide, we should show a simple bar chart: x-axis workload types (chat, summarization, embeddings), y-axis relative cost. Copy: "Workload-aware serving yields predictable unit economics."
Design-bot: Created draft slide template: https://figma.com/file/xyz/webinar-q2-draft (version 3).
Priya: Great. Legal: can we say "predictable unit economics" without extra qualifiers?
Legal: OK to use "predictable unit economics" if we add a footnote: "based on internal benchmarks under typical production mixes."
SDR-Leads: For the 1-pager, we need: three elevator lines, two rebut bullets, and a sample email cadences for webinar attendees. I can finalize after copy lock.
Carlos: Sample email cadence (drop here):
1) Day 0: Thanks + resource + CTA for self-serve trial
2) Day 3: Quick benchmark snapshot + offer for demo
3) Day 7: Case study link + ask to schedule
Jared: Also include a routing rule snippet for HubSpot: "webinar_q2=true -> assign to Inbound_Marketing; score>80 -> route to AE". Keep it human-friendly.
Priya: Can everyone drop their draft lines by EOD? We'll meet 9am tomorrow to finalize and hand to design.
Nina: Dropping mine now: 
- Cloud AI: "Platform breadth, unpredictable inferencing economics."
  Support: "Multiple customers report spikes under real mixes."
- LLM API: "Plug-and-play dev experience; limited production controls."
  Support: "No native KV-cache or rollout primitives in many APIs."
- Infra vendor: "Control at cost of building a serving runtime."
  Support: "Teams spend months tuning batching and quantization."
Carlos: Dropping headline variants for ads: 
- "Serve reliably. Pay less."
- "Cut inference waste. Ship faster."
Jared: Pushing a short demo script for AEs: 90-second talking points that show a live comparison of p95 latency and route fallback story.
Design-bot: Also exported a 6-word ad tile: "Run smarter inference. Keep costs low."
Priya: Awesome. Once drafts are in, I'll run a quick competitor name check with Legal. Tag me when updated. :rocket:
